subject: Lightning POC: setup milestones, access checklist, close runway
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@lumamed.com>, Anita Singh <anita.singh@lumamed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Lightning POC: setup milestones, access checklist, close runway

Hi Jordan / Anita —

Thanks again for the demo last week — excited to kick off a short, tightly scoped POC so you can validate latency and cost under a representative workload. To make this predictable on both sides I sketched a compact mutual action plan that gets us from kickoff -> activation -> acceptance in ~3 weeks. Please see attached MAP-Lightning-POC-v1.pdf and the network allowlist CSV template.

Summary of the POC scope (proposed):
- Duration: 3 weeks (validation + one acceptance window)
- Goals: Verify API latency SLO, embedding throughput for 1M calls/day equivalent, and end-to-end request fidelity vs your testset
- Environment: sandbox org (Redwood-managed tenants) + optional VPC peering for direct egress (if you want private peering)

Critical access items to complete in parallel (we need these by Day 3 to stay on the schedule):
1) Org setup: add a staging org and two seats for SRE/testing (we can create invites)
2) API keys: generate a staging API key and share via your secrets channel or our secure upload
3) IP allowlist: provide CIDRs for the allowlist (template attached)
4) VPC peering: if you choose peering, share preferred CIDR ranges and a primary network liaison

Proposed timeline (high-level):
- Day 0 (kickoff): confirm contacts and sign MAP
- Day 1–3: org invites, API key exchange, allowlist accepted
- Day 4–10: deploy queries & sampling, baseline runs
- Day 11–18: stress & throughput runs; collect logs & perf traces
- Day 19–21: review & acceptance window; decide next steps for Dedicated/Private

Ask: can you confirm who on your side will own org invites, who owns network (CIDR/contact), and whether you want VPC peering or simple IP allowlist for this run?

Attachments: [Attachment: MAP-Lightning-POC-v1.pdf (PDF)], [Attachment: network-allowlist-template.csv (CSV)]

Thanks — I can loop in our networking engineer (Marissa) and the SRE lead (Evelyn) once you confirm.

— Ava Chen
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0128

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@lumamed.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Lightning POC: setup milestones, access checklist, close runway

Hi Ava —

Appreciate the clear plan. A few quick clarifications before we lock dates: 

1) VPC peering: we'd prefer peering for data residency reasons, but need to confirm windows with our netops team. Can you confirm whether Redwood requires static outbound IPs on our side or only routing?

2) API keys: will you need a long-lived staging key or short-lived tokens? We are comfortable sharing a scoped key for the POC, but would rather not issue prod-equivalent keys.

3) CIDR ranges: our netops asks for an example CSV with the exact column names — I see you attached a template, thanks. Our point of contact is netops@lumamed.com (cc'd here).

If we agree on peering, can we aim for kickoff on Mon Nov 10 so our internal teams have time? Otherwise we can do the allowlist-only flow earlier.

Thanks,
Jordan Lee
Director of Platform Engineering
LumaMed Systems
jordan.lee@lumamed.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@lumamed.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Nov 2025 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Lightning POC: setup milestones, access checklist, close runway

Thanks Jordan — Marissa from Networking here, looping in a few operational details so we can avoid surprises. Quick notes: 

- Peering model: Redwood supports two peering models for MAPs: simple IP allowlist (fast, no routing changes) or VPC peering (private, requires CIDR planning + a 2-hour maintenance window to validate routes). If you choose peering we ask for a /24 minimum allocation for the peer side and a preferred maintenance window (US Pacific evenings are usually easiest).

- Static egress: we do not require static source IP ranges on your side when peering; traffic flows over the peering connection. For allowlist-only, we need the IPs your test runners will egress from (list in the CSV).

- Service accounts & IAM: for peering we recommend creating a service account with limited rights that we can use to sanity-check connectivity; we do not need broad admin privileges. If you prefer we can provide a checklist for the service account creation.

Proposed adjustments to the timeline if peering is chosen (keeping your initial 3-week validation):
- Nov 10 (Mon): Kickoff and network handoff 
- Nov 11–12: Netops exchanges: CIDRs, peering request, route tables configured
- Nov 13: Scheduled routing validation (2-hour window)
- Nov 14–20: Validation and perf runs
- Nov 21–23: Acceptance window

I'll drop a short network checklist in the shared Drive (link below) and I can coordinate the maintenance window with your netops contact.

Quick links: network checklist — https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cMAPdocs

— Marissa Cole
Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
[Attachment: network-allowlist-template.csv (CSV)]

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@lumamed.com>, Anita Singh <anita.singh@lumamed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, netops@lumamed.com
Date: Thu, 6 Nov 2025 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Lightning POC: setup milestones, access checklist, close runway

Jordan / Anita —

Great — thanks for the quick turnaround and for looping in netops. Based on Marissa's notes and your preference for peering, let's confirm the following and treat this as the executed MAP for the Lightning POC: 

Agreed items:
- Kickoff: Mon Nov 10, 11:00 PT (30-45m) — introductions, MAP sign-off
- Org invites: Redwood will send staging invites to the two SRE testers by Nov 11
- API keys: LumaMed will provide a scoped staging API key (short TTL acceptable) by Nov 11
- CIDRs: LumaMed to provide a /24 preferred CIDR and the allowlist CSV by Nov 11 (netops@lumamed.com)
- Peering: scheduled routing validation on Nov 13 in a 2-hour window (Marissa to coordinate exact slot)
- Acceptance window: Nov 21–23; final decision due by Nov 24

Open items / risk flags:
- SOC2 evidence: your security team may ask for SOC2-related artifacts during the acceptance run; please flag if that requires extra access or an NDA amendment
- Egress rules: ensure your firewall rules allow outbound HTTPS to our peering endpoint and TLS 1.2+

Next steps (action owners):
- Jordan / netops@lumamed.com: provide CIDR + allowlist CSV and preferred maintenance window (by EOD Nov 11)
- Marissa: will send the peering checklist and a sample service-account role in the next message
- Ava: will post the signed MAP to the shared Drive and provision initial staging keys for our side

Attachments: [Attachment: MAP-Lightning-POC-v1.pdf (PDF)], [Attachment: network-allowlist-template.csv (CSV)]

If that works, please reply with a one-line signoff ("Agree to MAP and dates") and we'll treat this as accepted. Thanks everyone — looking forward to a quick ramp.

— Ava Chen
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0128
